phases.label: Phase 1
phases.name: Foundation — v1.0 RC
phases.description: The current NestJS foundation: authentication, authorization, server lifecycle, Docker deployment, host metrics, and release automation.

items.text: Roles, account status, and MOD PBAC
Admin user management and last-admin protection
Server lifecycle and graceful RCON stop
Server visibility and access request workflow
CI/CD pipeline + GHCR edge/stable release channels

phases.label: Foundation / Next
phases.name: Stable-v1 Hardening
phases.description: Stable-v1 hardening is implemented and gated by unit, build, migration, e2e, and trusted real-Docker lifecycle checks. Its required seven-item scope is complete.

items.text: Stable API error envelope, machine codes, and request IDs
Resolve password semantics and bcrypt UTF-8 byte limits
Delete or wire dead login-throttle environment variables
Progressive login-abuse throttling using account + source context
Minecraft CPU quota and PIDs limit

phases.label: Phase 1.5
phases.name: Identity / Onboarding
phases.description: The required identity and onboarding scope is complete: Google authentication and linking, server visibility and access workflows, requestable discovery, and MOD granular permissions.

items.text: Google OAuth with challenge-bound local verification
Google account linking with explicit confirmation

phases.label: Phase 2A
phases.name: Platform Foundations
phases.description: The next backend milestone: framework-neutral foundations required by core operations and later integrations.

phases.label: Phase 3
phases.name: Core Operations
phases.description: The core Minecraft operations suite, built in dependency order on top of the stable backend and Phase 2A foundations.

items.text: Real-time server logs, stats, and player events
Scheduler foundation when scheduled operations first require it
Microsoft Minecraft account linking for player-management consumers
Offline player UUID linking with explicit offline-mode identity rules

phases.label: Phase 2B
phases.name: Integrations
phases.description: External consumers of the platform foundations. These remain secondary to the core Minecraft management path.

phases.label: Future Identity / Account Access
phases.name: Optional Follow-ons
phases.description: Optional account-access features that may be added after the core management experience is established.

items.text: [Optional] Magic-link authentication when SMTP is deliberately enabled

phases.label: Later
phases.name: Product Surfaces
phases.description: Later product capabilities whose detailed architecture will be defined only when they become active development targets.

phases.label: Backend 2.0
phases.name: Elysia 2
phases.description: Post-feature-completion, parity-first migration from NestJS when the final feature baseline is frozen and Elysia 2 with its required Bun ecosystem is production-ready.

items.text: Complete and freeze the final NestJS feature baseline
Document deferred functionality and synchronize all docs
Verify Elysia 2 ecosystem reliability on the selected Bun runtime
Port with route, status, body, auth, cookie, DB, Docker, and WS parity
